original_question: Study the scaling limit of the branchpoint structure in the fringe process associated with the critical beta-splitting model, viewed after rescaling as a point process describing branchpoint locations near a typical leaf.
target_in_paper: Open Problem 14 in Section 7.3 of the paper's July 5, 2024 v2 PDF: after discussing the relation between the global scaling limit CTCS(∞) and the local fringe distribution, the paper states that there should be a scaling limit of the discrete fringe process itself, with the limit representable as a point process of branchpoint positions.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the right problem almost exactly: it is about the critical beta-splitting model, the fringe process viewed from a typical leaf, and a further scaling limit whose natural description should involve branchpoint locations as a point process. That is the distinctive content of Open Problem 14, and it is narrower than the neighboring global-scaling questions about CTCS(∞).
missing_details: The paper's target is the scaling limit of the discrete fringe process itself, not directly the finite-n trees DTCS(n) or the global continuum object CTCS(∞).

You should specify the underlying discrete critical beta-splitting model DTCS(n): for each clade size m ≥ 2, the split m -> (i, m-i) occurs with probability q(m,i) = [m/(2 h_{m-1})]/[i(m-i)], where h_{m-1} = sum_{r=1}^{m-1} 1/r.
The relevant fringe object is the asymptotic fringe tree/process, defined as the n -> infinity local weak limit of DTCS(n) relative to a uniformly random leaf.

The paper gives an explicit description of that fringe tree in Section 4.2: ancestor clade sizes evolve by the reverse-HD chain with upward transition probabilities q^up(i,j) from equation (17), and at each jump i -> j the sibling clade is an independent DTCS(j-i) tree.
Your draft says 'near a typical leaf', but the paper's precise notion is 'relative to a uniformly random leaf' in the local-weak-limit sense.
The paper does not fix the exact rescaling, topology, or state space for the limit; determining these is part of the open problem.
The official formulation says only that the limiting object should be representable as a point process of branchpoint positions; it does not specify more structure than that.

The surrounding motivation is a local-versus-global consistency question: how the fringe distribution as a local limit should relate to the global scaling-limit object CTCS(∞), in analogy with the Brownian CRT.
No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or 'sufficiently large m' conditions are relevant here; the missing precision is entirely probabilistic and asymptotic.
refined_question: For the critical beta-splitting tree DTCS(n), in which each clade of size m ≥ 2 splits into subclades of sizes i and m-i with probability q(m,i) = [m/(2 h_{m-1})]/[i(m-i)] and h_{m-1} = sum_{r=1}^{m-1} 1/r, let F denote the asymptotic fringe tree/process, i.e. the local weak limit of DTCS(n) relative to a uniformly random leaf as n -> infinity. Determine an appropriate rescaling of this discrete fringe process and identify its scaling limit, making precise the paper's heuristic that the limiting object should be representable as a point process of branchpoint positions.
justification: The draft is best matched to Open Problem 14 because that is the only place where the paper explicitly asks for a scaling limit of the fringe process and immediately describes the expected limit as a point process of branchpoint positions. Section 4.2 supplies the exact meaning of the fringe process as the local weak limit relative to a typical leaf, while Section 7.3 explains that the problem is motivated by the Brownian-CRT phenomenon that local and global scaling limits are compatible. Section 5.6 is the nearby context showing that, in this model too, one can derive the fringe law from the global CTCS(∞) description, which is why the paper frames Open Problem 14 as a local/global consistency question rather than as a broad new scaling problem.
